name: Treaty wargames
question: Can a lab profit by cheating on a verified AI safety treaty?
summary: AI Race's Verified Race is a simulation of labs racing to deploy: each quarter every lab privately chooses safe or fast development, fast adds hidden catastrophe risk that hits everyone, and a treaty is enforced by audits, monitoring and sanctions. Its authors searched 35 covert-defection strategies and found these 14 treaty regimes deterred every one. Their own report says that does not prove no cleverer defection exists. Each regime is a target: find a covert strategy that profits against labs that comply, and the regime is shown not to be self-enforcing.
why: Whether an international agreement on AI development can be verified well enough that no party gains by cheating is a live governance question. Models like this one cannot settle it, since every number in them is invented, but they can show which verification designs fail and how. A found exploit is a concrete, reproducible counterexample.

source.title: Verified Race: a research environment inside AI Race
source.note: Parameters are invented, chosen so the race is a social dilemma; results are about mechanism, not the real world.
